function: DDPG sets the phase shifts of two cascaded IRSs in a THz uplink to maximize one user's rate under interference, or the sum rate (p. 2, 9).
system: Uplink at 300 GHz, 2 GHz bandwidth: two single-antenna users, single-antenna receiver, two cascaded passive reflecting IRSs of 18 elements each (p. 3, 11).
method: Deep reinforcement learning, DDPG with actor and critic networks (two hidden layers of 128 ReLU units), Adam, 10,000 training episodes per distance ratio (p. 9, 12).
data_channel: Own simulator: Rician fading (K=10) on user-IRS1 and IRS2-receiver links, correlated Rayleigh between IRSs, free-space plus THz absorption loss; 10^3 Monte-Carlo runs (p. 5, 11, 12).
test_conditions: DDPG trained separately for each distance ratio (11.53 hours, 10,000 episodes); results per distance ratio and correlation factor, with no unseen-scenario test (p. 12, 13).
baselines: Non-learned only: pseudo-inverse (Pinv) and block solution (BLS), exhaustive search and upper bound (M=N=4), random phases; no earlier learned method compared (p. 7, 12, 14).
metrics: Achievable rate of the desired user and sum rate (bits/s/Hz), reward convergence, and measured runtime of DDPG, BLS, Pinv (p. 12, 13, 14).
complexity: Forward-pass cost S*I+H*I*O+O*A+A versus Pinv O((MN)^2(M+N)), BLS, ES; measured 1000 iterations: DDPG 16.4 s, BLS 30.7 s, Pinv 947.5 s; training 11.53 h (p. 10, 11, 12).
q1_support: p. 5: "follow the Rician fading" model, and the IRS1-IRS2 channel is correlated Rayleigh (p. 5); custom simulator, with no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 12: "episodes for each distance ratio value", so a model is trained for each setting and no model is tested on an unseen one.
q3_support: p. 12: "We employ various methods, including DDPG, BLS, and Pinv solution"; p. 14 compares DDPG with ES, an upper bound, and random phases; all non-learned, and no earlier learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 10: "the cumulative complexity of the DDPG scheme is expressed as follows", compared with Pinv, BLS, ES orders (p. 11); p. 12 runtime: "16.421875 seconds for the DDPG".
q5_support: p. 12: "Our results were obtained through" 10^3 Monte-Carlo simulations of its own simulator; no code or data link and no public dataset.
notes: DDPG is retrained for each distance ratio, 11.53 hours each (p. 12). Fig. 10 varies learning rates of the same DDPG, which is not a learned baseline. The system has single-antenna users and receiver but two cascaded IRSs, so the system check passes. Tables 1 and 3 were read from page images.
